title.value: Stochastic Gradient Descent-Ascent and Consensus Optimization for Smooth Games: Convergence Analysis under Expected Co-coercivity
title.justification: The title is extracted directly from the paper's header, which clearly states the focus of the study on the convergence analysis of SGDA and SCO for smooth games.
title.quote: Stochastic Gradient Descent-Ascent and Consensus Optimization for Smooth Games: Convergence Analysis under Expected Co-coercivity

analysis.description: This paper explores the convergence analysis of two prominent algorithms, stochastic gradient descent-ascent (SGDA) and stochastic consensus optimization (SCO), under expected co-coercivity conditions for smooth games. The study introduces new theoretical guarantees for last-iterate convergence under these conditions, specifically for stochastic variational inequality problems that may be non-monotone. It suggests insights into minibatching complexity and proposes step-size strategies for achieving convergence to exact solutions.

type.justification: The paper primarily provides theoretical convergence guarantees and proposed changes to the SGDA and SCO algorithms without involving experimental or empirical results.
type.quote: In this work, we introduce the expected co-coercivity condition, explain its benefits, and provide the first last-iterate convergence guarantees of SGDA and SCO under this condition for solving a class of stochastic variational inequality problems.

name.justification: The paper focuses on optimization techniques like SGDA and SCO for solving variational inequality problems in machine learning contexts, linking closely to optimization research within deep learning.
name.quote: Motivated from the recent interest in solving adversarial formulations in machine learning such as generative adversarial networks (GANs), we consider in this paper a more abstract formulation of the problem and focus on solving the following unconstrained stochastic variational inequality (VI) problem.

name.justification: The paper discusses smooth games and optimization algorithms in the context of game theory, indicating a strong overlap with theoretical and algorithmic studies in game settings.
name.quote: Two of the most prominent algorithms for solving unconstrained smooth games are the classical stochastic gradient descent-ascent (SGDA) and the recently introduced stochastic consensus optimization (SCO).

name.justification: SGDA is explicitly mentioned as a focus of the research, including an exploration of its convergence properties under specified conditions.

is_contributed.justification: SGDA is a well-known algorithm and not introduced by this paper; the paper builds upon it but does not claim its invention.
is_contributed.quote: SGDA is known to converge to a stationary point for specific classes of games, but current convergence analyses require a bounded variance assumption.

is_executed.justification: The paper does not describe any actual implementation or execution of SGDA but discusses its theoretical properties.
is_executed.quote: We prove linear convergence of both methods to a neighborhood of the solution when they use constant step-size, and we propose insightful stepsize-switching rules.

is_compared.justification: SGDA is compared in terms of convergence guarantees with SCO in the theoretical findings of the paper.
is_compared.quote: We provide the first last-iterate convergence guarantees for stochastic gradient descent-ascent (SGDA) on (1) without any unrealistic noise assumption.
